verdicts.reason: A keeps a sane top-down order (logo, product, headline), but the legal line 'Flavours vary by region' is promoted to a near-headline subhead. The CTA is shrunk to chip size and dropped into the chip grid, so it doesn't stand out. The product is tiny and the chip rows press against the bottom edge. B scatters the chips randomly around the jar, buries an undersized CTA on the left, shrinks the logo into the bottom-left corner and also blows up the disclaimer.

A is the same scattered layout: chips float at arbitrary positions with no grid, the CTA is buried mid-left at chip size, the logo is a tiny bottom-left afterthought, and the disclaimer is oversized. B uses a deliberate split: logo and jar on the left, headline with the CTA and a neatly stacked chip column on the right. Its flaws are that the disclaimer is still far too large, the CTA is barely bigger than the chips, and the jar is small and floats low.

A has an organised structure: headline on top, the CTA and chips in one aligned right-hand column, and the jar on the left. But the disclaimer is enlarged into a subhead, the CTA is the same size as the chips, the logo sits awkwardly at the bottom centre, and the chip stack runs close to the bottom. B is the scattered layout again: no alignment, a buried CTA, a tiny logo in the corner and an oversized disclaimer.
